lines.text: The hall was as long as a church, and it was full of people.
They lay in rows on stone shelves, hundreds of them, one above another, like loaves in a bakery. Each of them held a small grey stone against their chest.
They weren't asleep. Their eyes were open. They just didn't look at anything.
From every stone, a thin thread of light ran down into a channel in the floor. The channels ran together into one stream, and the stream ran down through a grate, into the dark.
Tithe-stones. Like the one in the grey village. The College told us the tithe paid for the realm's wards. I believed them. I wrote essays about it.
Hobb had told me people vanished from the Lowmarket every winter. Debtors, mostly. Nobody ever asked where they went.
Now I knew.
Oswin had stopped beside one of the shelves. An old man lay there, grey as ash, with a miller's thick shoulders.
Jory. It's Jory, the miller of Ashby. They told us the ones who didn't burn were sent away to work off the debt.
Jory? It's Hale. Sir Oswin. Can you hear me?
Jory's eyes moved. Just a little, toward the sound of his name. Then they drifted away again.
At the far end of the hall, two Measurers walked the rows with their lenses, changing the stones like men changing candles.
Can I shoot them?
Yes. Later.
I meant it. Wren looked at me for a long moment. Then she nodded, and put the arrow back. She would hold me to it.
I wanted to wake every one of them. I wanted to carry them all out through the drain on my back. There were four hundred of them, and most of them couldn't stand.
If we tried, the alarm would ring before we got ten out. And then nobody would reach Ilse, or Maric's cure, or anyone at all.
It was the worst sum I have ever done.
We come back for them. All of them. I swear it.
I'll hold you to that, my lord. Ashby has waited long enough.
We followed the stream of light to the next stair. It ran down. Everything down here ran down.
At the bottom waited a row of iron doors, each with a mark cut into the stone above it. We counted to nine.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter ninety-seven, coming soon.
